channel.title: nexusEVnews
channel.description: Independent EV and renewable energy news, curated daily. Electric vehicles, solar, battery tech, and charging infrastructure.

item.title: Toyota's First-Ever Electric Hilux Takes On New Zealand's Off-Road Terrain
item.dc:creator: Ecotricity NZ
item.description: Fifty years in, Toyota has built its first fully electric Hilux. 144 kW, all-wheel drive, six off-road modes, and roughly 260 km of real-world range on the double cab. Tested on a dedicated off-road course in New Zealand.

item.title: 150 Solar Panels, 540 kWh of Storage, and a Cow Barn Running a Global Payments App
item.dc:creator: Victron Energy
item.description: Wietse Wind runs a payments app for 1.1 million users from a converted cow barn outside Amsterdam, powered entirely by solar and 540 kWh of Victron Energy storage. Four years, three system redesigns, and one flood.

item.title: The Pebble Flow Electric RV Has Hub Motors, Smart Glass, and an Auto-Dump System. It Also Works.
item.dc:creator: Out of Spec Reviews
item.description: Starting at $139,000, the Pebble Flow electric travel trailer pairs a 45 kWh LFP battery and two hub motors with automated hitching, leveling, and tank dumping. After a troubled experience with a competing trailer, 24 hours in with Pebble produced zero bugs.

item.title: Rivian R2 Configurator Is Open: The Trim Differences Are Bigger Than They Look
item.dc:creator: Travis Ketchum
item.description: Standard R2 buyers cannot add the factory tow package even as an option. Premium restores most of what Standard cuts for $5,500 more. Performance adds 656 hp and semi-active dampers. A full breakdown of where each trim makes or breaks the deal.

item.title: What Three Days Without a Car Taught One Rider About a $2,700 Electric Scooter
item.dc:creator: Mike O'Brien
item.description: The Segway GT3 Pro goes 50 mph, claims 86 miles of range, and costs $2,700. Mike O'Brien used it as his only vehicle for three days. The grocery run exposed the limits; everything else worked well.

item.title: Nine Days, Four Countries, One Electric Scooter: Paris to Monaco on a Dualron X
item.dc:creator: Chris Howett
item.description: A $7,000 Dualron X Limited, nine days, and nearly 1,180 km through France, Switzerland, Italy, and Monaco. A failing motor, three days of rain, and a battery reading zero with 6 km still to go. He made it.

item.title: Inside GM's 18-Month Bolt EV Sprint: How a Factory Pivots for One Final Run
item.dc:creator: Out of Spec Reviews
item.description: GM retooled the Fairfax plant in Kansas City in 10 months for an 18-month Bolt EV run. LFP batteries, an Equinox EV motor, and one shift a day. A factory visit that ended up on a live stream.

item.title: Walmart EV Charging Is Getting Credit Card Readers and Going Much Bigger Than Anyone Realized
item.dc:creator: The Arkansas eTraveler
item.description: Adam Happel confirms credit card terminals on every Walmart charger, 50 stations live, Walmart Plus discounts going national, and a curbside delivery pilot at charging stalls.

item.title: A $9,500 Starting Point Was Just the Beginning: Upgrading a Pivot Shuttle Amped for Real EMTB Use
item.dc:creator: Evans MTB Saga
item.description: After blowing through hubs, tires, and a drivetrain on a previous Avinox-powered bike, Evan rebuilds a base Pivot Shuttle Amped with parts finally rated for 130 Nm of motor torque.

item.title: Tampa to Atlanta in a Kia Niro: Can Mercedes Charging Fix EV Road Trips?
item.dc:creator: Everyday Chris
item.description: 612 miles, five Mercedes charger stops, no app required, $64.64 total. Every charger worked. The Kia Niro's 216-mile real-world range was the only real constraint on the trip.

item.title: Top Gear Calls the Ferrari Luce the Antidote to the Touchscreen Era
item.dc:creator: Top Gear
item.description: Physical toggles, rotary dials, a glass gear selector, and a screen that only pivots. Top Gear called the instrument dials the most beautiful ever fitted to a production car, and backed the Luce as the antidote to the touchscreen-and-button chaos defining most modern cars.

item.title: Ferrari's Own Story: Sixty Patents, 100 Engineers, and the Name That Means Light
item.dc:creator: Ferrari
item.description: Ferrari's own account of the Luce development: more than 60 patents filed, engineering closer to aircraft than conventional cars, and a name chosen because a car completely different in every possible way needed a name reflecting everything new.

item.title: Ferrari Luce by the Numbers: 700+ kW, 530 km Range, and an 800V Architecture That Charges 70 kWh in 20 Minutes
item.dc:creator: CarExpert
item.description: Four motors over 700 kW, 120 kWh battery, 350 kW DC charging, and 530 km claimed range in a 2.2-tonne car. CarExpert breaks down the full specification and asks the range question that needed asking.

item.title: The Two People Most Responsible for the Ferrari Luce Explain Why It Exists and Why It Looks Like Nothing Else
item.dc:creator: Cleo Abram
item.description: Jony Ive and Ferrari chief designer Flavio Manzoni explain why the Luce is a five-seat GT, why they rejected fake engine sound, and what the Purosangue parallel means for how this car will eventually be received.

item.title: Ferrari's First Electric Car Has No V12, No Fake Engine Sound, and Almost Nothing in Common With Any Ferrari Before It
item.dc:creator: Auto Focus
item.description: Auto Focus walks every inch of the Ferrari Luce: a five-seat quad-motor GT with 120 kWh, 300+ miles of range, active cooling vents, edge-parked wipers, and a cabin built entirely from metal, leather, and glass. No plastic. No fake engine sound.

item.title: Everrati’s Electric 964: The Iconic 911 Converted to Full Electric, Down to the Last Badge
item.dc:creator: Autotrader
item.description: Everrati replaced the flat-six in a 964-generation Porsche 911 with a 500-horsepower electric motor and 64 kWh battery. The RSR-tribute aero and RS 3.8 badging stay. The exhaust note doesn’t. All modifications are reversible.

item.title: Inside the Lordstown Endurance: One of Fewer Than 80 Ever Built, and One of Even Fewer Still on the Road
item.dc:creator: Aging Wheels
item.description: Lordstown Motors declared bankruptcy in 2023 after building somewhere between 56 and 80 trucks. One owner tracked down a road-legal example and has been driving it. It’s half-finished, fascinating, and may brick itself at any moment.

item.title: We Built the Tracker We Wish Existed When We Were Waiting for Our R1s
item.dc:creator: Jacob Hunka
item.description: People were reading website source code to find out when their Rivian was coming. Forum signatures listed Guide contact dates like military service records. We are not doing that again for the R2. The Rivian R2 Delivery Tracker is live.

item.title: Two Batteries, One Hitch, and the Case for All-Electric Glamping
item.dc:creator: Jacob Hunka
item.description: The Lightship AE1 carries its own 69 kWh battery and 80 kW motor to neutralize trailer drag on the tow vehicle. Paired with a Rivian, the real-world efficiency numbers are hard to argue with. This is what all-electric glamping looks like when the hardware actually works.

item.title: Atlanta, Rivian, and the Quiet Coincidence
item.dc:creator: Jacob Hunka
item.description: Atlanta has a failing air quality grade and a Rivian plant on its doorstep. A hypothetical about what one city could do with the electric mobility infrastructure that already exists — R2 autonomous taxis, ALSO cargo quads, e-bikes, and ZTL-style restricted zones — and what the health data says the stakes actually are. Includes data from the HEI lockdown air quality study (Chen et al., 2025) and the American Lung Association's 2025 Atlanta air quality report.
